items.title: AI-Native vs. Anti-AI Engineers
items.raw_excerpt: One of the key differences I an seeing between AI-native engineers and Anti-AI ones: the idea of "fully understanding" what you ship. Before LLMs, we did not fully understand the libraries we read, the kernels we touched, the networks we only grasped conceptually. We' have always been outsourcing intelligence to other engineers, teams, and systems for decades. One possible reason is that we use a library, we can tell ourselves we could read it. With an LLM, the fiction of potential understanding collapses. The real shift I am seeing isn't from "understanding" to "not understanding." It is towatds "I understand the boundaries, guarantees, and failure modes of what I'm responsible for." If agentic coding is the future, mastery becomes the ability to steer, constrain, test, and catch failures

excerpt_i18n.en: As generative AI fully enters the three-dimensional space, enabling machines not only to "see" objects but also to understand their structures, joints, and motion patterns has become a key focus for global research institutions and industries. From virtual content creation to robotic manipulation, and from digital twins to industrial simulation, the automated generation of movable 3D objects is regarded as a crucial foundational capability for future interactive digital worlds. However, existing methods are still largely constrained by reliance on complete 3D scans, inconsistencies arising from separate modeling of structure and texture, and difficulties in handling visibility changes caused by motion. In this context, a recent study by the S-Lab team at Nanyang Technological University offers a new solution. excerpt_i18n.en: According to Leifeng Network, on November 26, 2025, Qualcomm officially launched the fifth-generation Snapdragon 8 mobile platform. The debut of this new product marks the complete implementation of the Snapdragon 8 series' dual-flagship layout, which, together with the fifth-generation Snapdragon 8 Supreme Edition released in September, forms a differentiated positioning to jointly cover various demand scenarios in the high-end mobile chip market. As a core new member of the Snapdragon flagship product portfolio, the fifth-generation Snapdragon 8, with its new positioning, achieves comprehensive breakthroughs in six core dimensions: performance, energy efficiency, AI, imaging, gaming, and connectivity, precisely meeting consumers' diverse needs for high-end mobile experiences. Single-core performance is improved by 35%.
excerpt_i18n.es: Según informa Leifeng, el 26 de noviembre de 2025, Qualcomm lanzó oficialmente la plataforma móvil Snapdragon 8 de quinta generación. En concreto, el Snapdragon 8 Elite de quinta generación se centra en el mercado ultra premium por encima de 5000 yuanes, diseñado específicamente para dispositivos insignia de máximo rendimiento, con configuraciones clave como CPU Oryon de alta frecuencia de 4.6 GHz, 18 MB de memoria dedicada para GPU y arquitectura de segmentación completa. Por su parte, el Snapdragon 8 de quinta generación cuenta con una frecuencia principal de CPU de 3.8 GHz.
